title: Winter ice gave no clear added May-November evaporation prediction gain at Lake Superior in 1995-2022
abstract: We tested whether winter maximum ice cover adds information about May-November net evaporation at Lake Superior. The reference model used year, prior May-November evaporation and current January-March evaporation. Each fit used earlier years only. We used L2SWBM v2023.2 monthly medians and a fixed NOAA GLERL ice table, with 28 test years in 1995-2022. Adding ice reduced mean squared error by 8.84%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -50.71% to +47.72%. RMSE fell from 63.181 to 60.323 mm. Every planned check interval included zero. Omitting one scored year gave gains from -4.69% to +18.07%. All fitted ice slopes were negative, but the test does not establish added prediction value. It does not show that ice has no physical effect. One lake, few test years, shared model inputs, revised reconstructions and omitted joint posterior uncertainty limit inference. This is a retrospective benchmark, not a real-time forecast. The package includes original code, aggregate results, resampling draws, source hashes, independent checks and a figure. Source tables and annual records stay external.

display.caption: Ice predictor scores for 28 test years, 1995-2022. Positive values mean a reduction in mean squared error. Lines are conditional 95% percentile intervals. The primary row uses five-year circular blocks and L2SWBM v2023.2. Every interval includes zero. Other rows are descriptive checks with no correction for multiple comparisons.
